title: The Sordid History of Bachelor/Bachelorette Parties
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history of bachelor and bachelorette parties, from pre-wedding rituals across cultures (Swedish muk vlaar, Scottish Blackening, Belgian bridal shower origin story) through the late nineteenth-century bachelor dinner and the 1890s-1900s "Awful Seely Dinner" scandal in New York, Emily Post's rebuttal, and the rise of hen/him parties, Chippendales-driven bachelorette culture, and later delayed marriages. They cover movies (Bachelor Party, The Hangover, Bridesmaids, Rough Night), kidnapping and prank traditions, rising costs tied to Instagram, and modern alternatives like camping trips. The episode opens with a promo for Man Guesh's new podcast Obsessions: Wild Chocolate, and ends with listener mail and a preview of that show.

segments.title: Opening banter and Obsessions promo
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode, promote Man Guesh's new podcast Obsessions: Wild Chocolate, and chat about Boston, a Kevin Can F**k Himself mention, and a pavement show.

segments.title: Origins of bachelor parties and the hosts' views
segments.summary: The hosts describe the French name for bachelor parties and how late-nineteenth-century bachelor parties arose when grooms often married as virgins. They discuss the tension between modern bachelor parties and their original purpose, and cite a 2016 ethnographic study of European bachelor parties where participants found them unenjoyable.

segments.title: Bachelor party evolution and cheating warnings
segments.summary: The hosts argue that modern bachelor parties are driven by a small group of hard-partying friends and are shifting toward camping and retreats. They discuss the idea of celebrating the groom as an individual and warn against cheating at parties, citing anecdotal stories of weddings called off after bachelor party misbehavior.

segments.title: Pre-wedding traditions across cultures
segments.summary: Josh introduces pre-wedding rituals worldwide, including the mikvah, ancient Greek offerings, the Swedish muk vlaar virgin-night celebration and its 1669 ban in Uppsala, and the Scottish Blackening, where the bride and groom are mock-kidnapped and covered in messy substances.

segments.title: Industrialization and the origins of modern bachelor parties
segments.summary: The hosts cite sociologist Thomas Turnell Read's argument that industrialization and city factory life produced new rites of passage, such as drinking and practical jokes, that evolved into bachelor and bachelorette parties.

segments.title: The Awful Seely Dinner scandal
segments.summary: The hosts recount the Awful Seely Dinner, a privately hosted party in New York for Clinton Seely's bachelor dinner at Sherry's, which involved dancers including Little Egypt. Police raids, a court case, and public scandal followed, and Little Egypt's later life is described. Emily Post's later claim that such dinners were staid is contrasted with a first-person account of a Rhode Island stag party.

segments.title: Bridal showers and the rise of hen and him parties
segments.summary: The hosts explain the origins of the bridal shower in sixteenth-century Belgium, the British ribbon girl tradition, the 1960s-70s shift to personal showers, and the early-1990s UK hen and him party trend.

segments.title: Bachelorette party history and the Chippendales effect
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how the Chippendales show in Los Angeles helped kick off bachelorette parties in the US, the term's appearance in a New York Times article, and how later marriage and greater disposable income fueled bigger, more commercial parties. They reference Diane Tye's interviews comparing 1990s planning with 2000s party-company scripts.

segments.title: Party antics, movies, and the Hangover era
segments.summary: The hosts share personal bachelor and bachelorette party stories and discuss movies including Bachelor Party, How to Murder Your Wife, The Hangover, Very Bad Things, Bridesmaids, and Rough Night.

segments.title: Kidnapping, pranks, and the costs of parties
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Australian bucks party kidnappings, the David Boyer account of a fake broken-leg prank, and a Savings.com survey putting average bachelor party costs around fifteen hundred dollars and bachelorette parties around nine hundred, with Instagram cited as a driver of spending.

segments.title: Listener mail and Diarrhea Planet
segments.summary: The hosts read a listener email about postpartum depression and finding comfort in the podcast, and mention an invitation from the band Diarrhea Planet.

segments.title: Obsessions: Wild Chocolate preview
segments.summary: A preview of the Obsessions: Wild Chocolate podcast, hosted by Rowan Jacobson, about a German cacao hunter's search for wild cacao in the Bolivian Amazon.
